title: The Grain Code residual-area criterion was taught as one of its three limits, and the Part B assumed shifted surface was taught as the ship's rolling amplitude
candidate_claim: Founder/GPT independent high-risk review of the published corpus. QB2_A#q11 and #q33 reduce the Grain Code residual-area criterion to, in substance, 'area up to 40 degrees'. QB2_A#q11 describes the grain surface after shifting as 'an angle matching the rolling amplitude'. QB2_A#q11's Casualty Link uses MV Leros Strength as grain casualty support when she was laden with approximately 18,000 t of apatite. QB2_A#q11's On My Vessel block asserts a Maersk geared bulk fleet carrying agricultural bulk, which is not established Founder experience.
candidate_verdict: UPHELD ON ALL FOUR, AND THE FIRST TWO WERE READ FROM THE INSTRUMENT RATHER THAN ACCEPTED ON REPORT. The Grain Code as adopted is held in the corpus as the annex to resolution MSC.23(59) (SRC-GRAINCODE-MSC23-59), and A 7.1.2, B 1.3, B 1.5, B 2.3, B 3.2.1, B 3.3, B 4 and B 5.1 were each read off the page before anything was changed. The residual-area defect is not cosmetic: on many grain loading conditions the governing limit is the angle of maximum difference between the ordinates of the two curves, which falls well before 40 degrees, so a candidate stating the old form computes the wrong area. The 15-second answer on q11 was examined and DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE - it never stated the limit, so it had nothing wrong in it to correct.

authority.instrument: IMO resolution MSC.23(59), Adoption of the International Code for the Safe Carriage of Grain in Bulk, with the Code as adopted in its annex. Held at F:/RulesApp-Local-Input/true-source/03-imo-instruments/Grain-Code/_base-and-amendments/IMO_resolution_MSC.23-59_grain_code_as_adopted.pdf, sha256 5b2107d304bcfd8ad6c5cc080c33a94a9d168b5aaa3895277c61134e6cad8678, registered as SRC-GRAINCODE-MSC23-59.
authority.access_note: The PDF is a scan of the 1991 printed resolution with an OCR text layer carrying visible artefacts ('ahall' for 'shall', 'betveen' for 'between'). Every provision quoted below was located through the text layer and then read against the page image. Substance is asserted; byte-verbatim OCR strings are not.
authority.operative_text_A_7_1_2: p.5: '.2 in the statical stability diagram, the net or residual area between the heeling arm curve and the righting arm curve up to the angle of heel of maximum difference between the ordinates of the two curves, or 40 degrees or the angle of flooding, whichever is the least, shall in all conditions of loading be not less than 0.075 metre-radians'
authority.operative_text_A_7_1_1: p.5: '.1 the angle of heel due to the shift of grain shall not be greater than 12 degrees or in the case of ships constructed on or after 1 January 1994 the angle at which the deck edge is immersed, whichever is the lesser'
authority.operative_text_A_7_1_3: p.5: '.3 the initial metacentric height, after correction for the free surface effects of liquids in tanks, shall be not less than 0.30 m'. NOTE: this is the GRAIN CODE's criterion. The card's Key Numbers block had attributed the 0.30 m to SOLAS VI, which is the chapter that makes the Code mandatory, not the source of the figure. That was the third pre-existing defect CORR-GRAIN-MSC552-20260831 registered and is corrected here.
authority.operative_text_B_2_3: p.24, 'ASSUMED VOLUMETRIC HEELING MOMENT OF A FILLED COMPARTMENT, TRIMMED': '2.3 The resulting grain surface after shifting shall be assumed to be at 15 degrees to the horizontal.'
authority.operative_text_B_3_2_1: p.27: in filled compartments, untrimmed, exempted from trimming outside the periphery of the hatchway under A 10.3.1, '.1 the resulting grain surface after shifting shall be assumed to be at an angle of 25 degrees to the horizontal. However, if in any section of the compartment, forward, aft, or abreast of the hatchway the mean transverse area of the void in that section is equal to or less than the area which would obtain by application of B 1.1, then the angle of grain surface after shifting in that section shall be assumed to be 15 degrees to the horizontal'
authority.operative_text_B_3_3: p.28: in filled compartments, untrimmed, exempted from trimming in the ends under A 10.3.2, the surface abreast of the hatchway after shifting is at 15 degrees and the surface in the ends at 25 degrees to the horizontal.
authority.operative_text_B_4_note: p.28, note on figure B 4: 'If the wing spaces in way of the trunk cannot be properly trimmed in accordance with A 10, it shall be assumed that a 25 degree surface shift takes place.'
authority.operative_text_B_5_1: p.28, 'ASSUMED VOLUMETRIC HEELING MOMENT OF A PARTLY FILLED COMPARTMENT': '5.1 When the free surface of the bulk grain has not been secured in accordance with A 16, A 17 or A 18, it shall be assumed that the grain surface after shifting is at 25 degrees to the horizontal.'
authority.operative_text_B_1_3_and_B_1_5: p.23: where the Administration authorises account to be taken of assumed underdeck voids in a filled compartment, trimmed, 'total heeling moment: 1.06 x calculated transverse heeling moment'; and '1.5 In partly filled compartments the adverse effect of the vertical shift of grain surfaces shall be taken into account as follows: total heeling moment: 1.12 x calculated transverse heeling moment.'
why_the_old_wording_is_wrong: A 7.1.2 states THREE upper limits joined by 'whichever is the least'. The card carried only the second. The area actually required is therefore the smallest of the three, and the maximum-difference angle commonly governs.

Part B nowhere models the ship's roll. Every angle in it is an ASSUMED grain surface after shifting, prescribed per compartment configuration, and the values differ (15 and 25 degrees, and both within a single untrimmed compartment under B 3.3). Teaching one universal angle, or teaching it as the rolling amplitude, misdescribes what the calculation is.
NO NEW LEGAL EFFECT IS ASSERTED. Every figure added is quoted from the instrument with its clause; nothing is inferred.
authority.leros_strength: MV Leros Strength (1997) was carrying approximately 18,000 t of apatite and was lost to structural failure. She is not evidence of a grain-shift stability failure. This was ALREADY registered as a pre-existing defect by CORR-GRAIN-MSC552-20260831, which deliberately left it for the correction queue; the independent review reached the same conclusion, and this record closes it. NO SUBSTITUTE CASUALTY WAS SOUGHT OR INVENTED - the block now says no specific casualty is necessary to answer this question.
authority.on_my_vessel: The Founder's sea time is on Maersk A/S container vessels. A Maersk geared bulk fleet carrying agricultural bulk is not established experience and was removed. The replacement asserts only what is true: that bulk grain is not a cargo regime he operates, that the Grain Code does not apply to his ship, and that the examination expects the principle rather than the practice. No Maersk cargo practice is invented.
